challenges.name: thin-controllers-errors-quiz
challenges.title: Which layer owns the rule, and which filter catches the error?
challenges.description: A global exception filter for domain errors, and a business rule that lives in a controller while a background job calls the service directly. Decide whether each statement is True or False.

questions.explanation: False. @Catch(DomainError) limits the filter to exceptions that are instances of DomainError; registering it globally only means it applies to every route, not to every exception. A TypeError is not a DomainError, so Nest's built-in global exception filter handles it and answers 500 with { "statusCode": 500, "message": "Internal server error" }, logging the error on the server. The misconception is that "global" widens what a filter catches. A @Catch() with no arguments would catch everything - and would then also have to handle HttpExceptions such as the ValidationPipe's 400, or it would turn them into 500s.

True. The controller is only one entry point into the enrollment rules; the CSV job, a queue consumer or an admin script call the service directly and skip every check that lives in a controller. Rules about the domain (published, prerequisites, duplicates) belong in the service, which throws a domain error such as CourseNotPublishedError; each entry point then decides how to report it - the HTTP layer maps it to 404, the job logs and skips the row. The misconception is that the controller is a safe place for rules because "all requests go through it"; not every caller is a request.

challenges.name: map-domain-errors
challenges.title: Map domain errors to HTTP in one place
challenges.description:
CodeDev's EnrollmentService (given, do not change) holds the enrollment rules and throws domain errors that know nothing about HTTP. Write the HTTP side: one mapping function, like a global NestJS exception filter, and two thin controller handlers.

mapError(thrown) returns { statusCode, error, message }. Decide with instanceof, so a subclass maps like its parent; never by error names or message text:
- NotFoundError and its subclasses (CourseNotFoundError, LessonNotFoundError) -> 404, "Not Found", the error's message.
- AlreadyEnrolledError -> 409, "Conflict", the error's message.
- PrerequisiteMissingError -> 422, "Unprocessable Entity", the error's message (the request is well-formed; a business rule is not met yet).
- CourseNotPublishedError -> 404, "Not Found", message "Course <courseId> not found" (a draft course must look exactly like one that does not exist).
- ValidationFailedError -> 400, "Bad Request", message = its details array.
- Anything else - another Error, a DomainError subclass not listed above, or a thrown value that is not an Error (a string, null, a plain object) -> 500, "Internal Server Error", message "Internal server error". Never put the internal message in a 500.

enrollHandler(req, service) for POST /v1/enrollments: call service.enroll(req.userId, req.body.courseId) and return { status: 201, body: <the enrollment> }.
unenrollHandler(req, service) for DELETE /v1/enrollments/:courseId: call service.unenroll(req.userId, req.params.courseId) and return { status: 204, body: null }.
The handlers do not catch anything: the test runner plays the framework, calls mapError for whatever a handler throws and answers { status: statusCode, body: <the mapped body> }.

The test runner either maps a list of thrown values and prints the bodies, or sends a list of requests through the handlers and prints the responses, as JSON.
hints: What does the learner's browser need from a 500, and what does the on-call engineer need? Only one of them should ever see "connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.5:5432". And what does a value that is not an Error at all - a thrown string or null - have in common with a TypeError?

Write mapError as a chain of instanceof checks, one per row of the table, ending in a single fallback for everything else. instanceof NotFoundError is already true for CourseNotFoundError, so subclasses need no extra branch; a plain object with name "NotFoundError" is not an instance and must fall through. The handlers are one service call each plus the success status.

The same shape for a different module: a payments filter maps CardDeclinedError (and subclasses such as InsufficientFundsError) to 402 with its message, and PaymentNotFoundError to 404. A thrown "gateway timeout" string, or new Error("socket hang up"), falls through every instanceof check and becomes { statusCode: 500, error: "Internal Server Error", message: "Internal server error" }, while the original error is only written to the server log.

tests.name: Domain errors map to 404, 409 and 422 with their own messages
Enroll 201, enroll again 409, leave 204, leave again 404
A draft course answers 404 without revealing it exists; an unknown course is 404 as well
An empty courseId is 400 with the details array; a missing prerequisite is 422

message: courseId must be a non-empty string

tests.name: Unknown errors and unmapped domain errors are 500 and never leak the internal message
Thrown non-Error values (a string, null, a look-alike plain object) are 500
Subclasses map like their parent; ValidationFailed keeps every detail in order

details: plan must be one of: free, premium

message: plan must be one of: free, premium
